$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $\mathbf{b}$ shown above. Find the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\!A\mathbf{x}=W\mathbf{b}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\!A\mathbf{x}=W\mathbf{b},$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\!A)^T{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132108/assets/6cbd613ac7478ba1fde06ded31ef473e3cdbc8639a9c134d853cbac8b0518334.svg)

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 36\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}21 & -21 \\ -21 & 21\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-39 \\ 39\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}21 & -21 & -39 \\ -21 & 21 & 39\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}21 & -21 & -39 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
x_1=-\dfrac{13}{7}+x_2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is
